faces.f: Weather is more predictable than the Izzet.

"It is forbidden. Asking why is irrelevant."
—Sergiu, Opal Lake magistrate
With the Izzet occupied elsewhere, many of their public works fell into disrepair.
A bargain in Keyhole Downs is always too good to be true.
Information travels quickly through Ravnica's network of messengers and thought agents.
The Izzet specialize in unnatural disaster.

"Civilization will subsume us unless we overwhelm it instead."
—Speaker Zegana
One piercing stare usually convinces thieves to go elsewhere.
Many Tin Street shops display a sign on the door: "No cloaks allowed."
As whispers and rumors increased, so did the demand for fail-safe barriers.

"To prevent action is to prevent transgression."
—Azorius Arrester motto

"Day 31: I finally succeeded in my time reversal experiment!
"Day 30: I might have a problem here."
—Journal of the Prime Izmagnus

"Obviously, the Firemind's mission is worth more than a few goblins."
—Pelener, chamberlain of Niv-Mizzet
An elocutor forces criminals to confess to the laws they merely intended to break.
In the hands of the open-minded, a runewing quill writes wisdom of its own.

"It will dodge your first arrow and flatten you before there's a second."
—Alcarus, Selesnya archer
"I've dreamt of the future, Isperia. Danger is on the horizon. You must heed my warning."
The Dimir would hire her, if only they knew where she lived. The Azorius would condemn her, if only they knew her name.
"Patience, mage. Killing you now would be too easy."
The first motion put forth in the pristine Jelenn Column was for severe restrictions on the airspace around New Prahv.

"He makes up his own laws, and that's dangerous to all who love peace and prosperity. Kill him on sight."
—Mirela, Azorius hussar
When Selesnya missionaries moved into the Shanav Quarter, they faced scorn, ridicule, and ultimately martyrdom.

"The entire murder scene was covered in dripping, oozing slime. No need for a soothsayer to solve that one."
—Pel Javya, Wojek investigator

"Without a body, the soul is helpless to fight the terms of our contracts."
—Somhaur, Orzhov pontiff
One of the many reasons why open-air markets close at dusk.
The murderer faced justice in the Azorius courts, but his soul was set free on a technicality.
He's the unlife of the party.
Everyone knew the Dimir had done the damage. Everyone suspected the Izzet had hired them.
"You just need the right incentive to fulfill my dreams."
When times are tough, the poor eat the rats. When times are tougher, the rats eat the poor.
He'll point you to your death row seats.
Life's too short to not do the things you love.
With no memories left to compare to his present situation, Andalum was finally content.
"Jarad fancies himself king of the undercity, but he's merely king of rot."
It took three years for it to occur to him to use the chain as a weapon, but once it did, he made up for lost time.
There are some shadows that even the Dimir fear.
A gargoyle's voice reaches pitches that will shatter glass and warp bone.
It's sent into unguilded districts by the Orzhov to collect the souls of those no one will miss.
Rakdos cultists are her best customers. They never flinch at pain and are seldom good at math.

"We follow it through its tunnels, and where it dies, we farm."
—Mihas, spore druid
As the bounty on Massacre Girl rose, so did the number of imitators.

"Let him be an example to others who would default on their debts to us."
—"The Cozen," Orzhov assassin
If you're looking for it, it's available. The question is how much you're willing to pay.

"The most impressive performances can be done only once."
—Mote, Rakdos madcap
"Smarter than death? Let's see you outsmart my mace, necromancer!"
Novice shopkeeps spend hours deciding how best to display their wares. Veterans focus on portability.
As the price of wood and coal rose, smiths found creative ways to keep their forges burning.
The star performer of the Juri Revue, his shows have fans and blood spilling into the street.
The most ancient streets take on a life of their own. A few have decided to move to nicer neighborhoods.
Nothing evens the odds like a little lightning.

"Such boorish noise is what passes for subtlety among the Boros."
—Vraska
You don't so much hire goblins as put ideas in their heads.
If the pig's blood drips on you, you're next on the chain.
He wants to watch Ravnica burn, one soul at a time.
It's easier to just aim at everything.
The smelting district is home to many who see the guilds as not for them.

"Watch the voltage. We don't need another charred, crashing viashino."
—Bori Andon, Izzet blastseeker

"The Izzet are an equation that turns lunacy into explosions."
—Leonos, Azorius arbiter
Close finishes are settled by who can dismount and get to weapons first.
The mask isn't meant to hide his identity. It's meant to keep the viscera out of his eyes.
Goblins and architects seldom get along.
Nothing was going to stop it—not the narrow alleys, not the Boros garrison, and certainly not the four-story Orzhov cathedral.
Joining the Worldsoul took years of study and meditation. Severing that connection took the snap of Rakdos's fingers.
The fear of dragons is as old and as powerful as the fear of death itself.
Beauty is in the eye of the exploder.
"You may call me a fool, selling this stuff on Orzhov turf. Well, you need to be a little reckless to survive."
In the towering trees of the Samok Stand and the predators that guard them, the might of the Ravnican wild has returned.
The silk of the archweavers adds structural integrity to otherwise unstable Izzet building sites.
Only a worthy few are permitted within the sentient forest known as Axebane.

"When the spires have burned and the cobblestones are dust, he will take his rightful place as king of the wilds."
—Kirce, Axebane guardian
Magistrate Ludy agreed to designate land for the brushstriders only after several broken windows and dozens of missing blini-cakes.
The farther they go from Vitu-Ghazi, the less willing the crowd is to part for them.

"In each of us is the strength of all of us."
—Trostani
Some Golgari insects live for centuries—and they never stop growing.

"We traffic in flesh, not souls. Still, it's a shame to let anything go to waste."
—Cevraya, Golgari shaman
The Street Swarm is the labor class that drives the Golgari's endless cycle of life and death.
"So many oppose us, but we are the reed that bends without breaking."
Every inch of Ravnica is home to something.

"The prohibition of unnecessary tossing of the citizenry by giants shall also extend to spontaneous giants."
—Isperia's Edict, provision VII.789.2
The furious citizens blamed the Simic for releasing it in their district. The Simic pointed out that rats were no longer a problem.

"The Selesnya are gathering armies. Do you still believe they aren't preparing for war?"
—Teysa, to Isperia
The city is vast and perilous, but there are places where a weary traveler can feel very much at home.
The trouble started when a street urchin bet a goblin he could ride one until the clock on Shilbo's Tower struck thirteen.
Gruul warriors never need to be stirred to battle. They need only to be shown where the battle is.
Raked by vertical spikes of glass and stone, Ravnica's vistas offer only a rare glimpse of the horizon.

"Give me enough refuse and mana and I will summon an ooze that can engulf all of Ravnica."
—Cevraya, Golgari shaman
The Izzet's plans to exploit the undercity ran into a few stubborn obstacles.
It chases its airborne prey relentlessly, heedless to what it pulverizes beneath its hooves.
The ruins of Old Prahv became a wildspace, although all birdsong was silenced by lingering Azorius magic.
"When they covered the world in city, all they did was give themselves nowhere to run."
The Izzet quickly suspended their policy of lifetime guarantees.
No one in the Conclave acts alone.

"Finally, a weapon the Boros can't confiscate!"
—Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue

"The rules of logic and order have already made the choice for you."
—Isperia
Centaurs are sent to evangelize in Gruul territories where words of war speak louder than prayers of peace.
Its favorite treats are candied hands and sweet hearts.
Instructors at the Kasarna training grounds are capable healers in case their students fail to grasp the subtleties of combat.
Senators of Azorius often hired agents to spy on the Selesnya. They were told to record every spore and root they saw, as each could become a deadly foe.
Wolf riders hone their skills traversing the perilous rooftops, each dizzying step bringing elf and wolf closer together.
Weakness is not in the nature of the Swarm.
Bleak rumors reached Trostani's ears. She decreed that no one should travel alone.

"I never thought I'd be so glad to see two tons of beak and claws bearing down on me at the speed of an arrow."
—Mirela, Azorius hussar
In Rakdos-controlled neighborhoods, everyone is part of the show.

"The other guilds will learn the hard way not to interfere with our investigations."
—Bori Andon, Izzet blastseeker
"My ruling is final. Order is upheld. Justice is done."
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."

"Let the rest of Ravnica sneer. One way or another, they all end up in the undercity."
—Jarad
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.

"We can't control enemies who have no regard for their own survival."
—Arrester Lavinia, Tenth Precinct
They share no bloodline, but a bond greater than family unites them. Such are the gifts of the Worldsoul.

"You think no one is watching, you think you're smart enough to escape, and most foolish of all, you think no one cares."
—Arrester Lavinia, Tenth Precinct

"Even this primitive specimen of my kind is impressive."
—Niv-Mizzet
"I serve only justice. But through that duty, I serve all of Ravnica."
"The Izzet are searching for something. Discern what or die trying."
He lurks in the undercity, eager for the corpse haulers to unload their rotting cargo.
What some see as "distracted" is really "fathoming the unfathomable."
"The only action worth taking is one with an unknown outcome."
He has no patience for minds that do not inspire him or explode by trying.

"Let all feel joy in pain."
—Rakdos
Ragemutts pull the chariots of the Butcher Clowns, a trio of wingless, zombified faeries formerly of the Izzet.
When Lord Rakdos stirred from his slumber, everyone else's nightmare began.
When one of the great guardians arises, it sweeps enemies aside like chaff yet takes care not to crush a single insect underfoot.
Don't cross a Devkarin elf unless you long for an early grave.
Insatiable, irresistible, and insane.
"And would you care to explain why your satchel is radiating an aura of unstable energy?"

"We could never accept anyone with a face that pretty or a mind that sane."
—Nyoser, Gore-House ringleader

"Try not to look guilty. Or delicious."
—Thorpe, street urchin

"Straight from the blood-drenched imagination of our illustrious parun!"
—Nyoser, Gore-House ringleader
"Let the knowledge of absolute law inspire you to live a life of absolute order."
Leonos had no second thoughts about the abolishment edict. He'd left skyrunes warning of the eviction, even though it was cloudy.
"If this is thinking, I don't know what I was doing before."
Gorgons crave beautiful things: gems, exquisite amulets, the alabaster corpses of the petrified dead . . .
Unwelcome in Golgari colonies, he found his own dark place from which to represent the Swarm.
"Preachers of freedom forget that conformity can be beautiful."
Azorius lawmages would like to outlaw the creation of weirds, but first they'd have to settle their long-standing debate on how to classify them.
Although Cryptwitch Merree vanished after a spat with Rakdos, her playthings lingered.
"We will defend the Worldsoul from Izzet 'progress' at any cost."
Many chemisters are oblivious to the innumerable machinations of their guild, instead focusing obsessively on creating the perfect weird.
Despite its enormous stature, it can fold itself into a tunnel with startling quickness, vanishing back into the undercity.

"We will grow an army large enough to withstand the Izzet's madness."
—Trostani

"It misses nothing and it has no sense of humor."
—Barvisa, courtroom scribe
When it escaped, the experimenters hesitated. It would cause untold havoc, yet they wished to see it in action.
Devil-blades and dripping blood make music Rakdos never tires of hearing.
"If there were such a thing as a soul, I think it would be behind the gallbladder but above the kidneys."

"It makes better use of Uncle Dragi's head than he ever did."
—Pesha, retired blacksmith

"One day every pillar will be a tree and every hall a glade."
—Trostani
For the Azorius, the opportunity to serve the law is too great an honor for death to interrupt.

"The higher the mind soars, the greater its understanding of the law."
—Isperia
Dimir mages put the lanterns to good use, creating shapeshifters and sleeper agents from mana foreign to them.
Those without a guild signet often display a different form of protection.
Like a single ant, it only hints at the colony below.
The fearful want the procedure before a blood festival. The guilty seek it afterward.
The Rakdos use it for everything you can think of and plenty more than that.
A mark of unity when you want one; a fierce guardian when you need one.
The sweepers roam endlessly, scrubbing away the refuse—and anything else too slow or too clumsy to get out of their way.
It is rumored the Azorius paid an exorbitant sum to ensure its symbol would appear at the top.
Enter the Senate, the seat of justice and the foundation of Ravnican society.
Where the dead serve as diversion, decor, and dessert.
Enter those who are starving and sick. You are welcome among the Swarm when the rest of Ravnica rejects you.
A place to relax, if you have the proper permit.
Enter those with the vision to create and the daring to release their creations.
The best funeral shroud is the fabric of new life.
Enter and indulge your darkest fantasies, for you may never pass this way again.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
Enter and rejoice! The Conclave stands united, open to one and all.
Crafted with genius, energized with madness.
In the gardens of the Conclave, order and beauty are the roots of power.

"If we cannot have peace, we will have justice."
—Aurelia
The Dimir agents watched from the shadows. "Eight hours, and I've yet to see him blink," Nefara hissed. "I suggest we find another way in."
"Law is the light of civilization."
"You have the right to remain silent. Mostly because I tire of your excuses."
"Your potential to commit a crime warrants further investigation."
"None may pass . . . for free."

"Through the haze of battle I saw the glint of sun on golden mane, the sheen of glory clad in mail, and I dropped my sword and wept at the idiocy of war."
—Dravin, Gruul deserter
"By the time your knees have worn through your robe, you may have begun to learn your place."

"First, you must fight among the rank and file. It is there I will discern your skills as a leader."
—Aurelia, to Gideon Jura

"Where did *she* come from? More importantly, are there more like her?"
—Gideon Jura
Her enemy's strength is her own.
Equenauts are the seeds of the Conclave, scattered on the four winds, searching for new places to take root.

"No doubt the arbiters would put you away, after all the documents are signed. But I will have justice now."
—Alovnek, Boros guildmage
Into the light the good are welcomed, and with the light the evil are banished.

"What root and branch cannot reach, our winged friends will attend to."
—Zunak, Selesnya strategist

"I watched its blade swing through me, but I was hollow, empty. I saw its face contort in rage but could not hear it snarl."
—Klattic, Boros legionnaire
Some souls are too damaged to be of use to the Orzhov.
Their ranks are thin, their formation is improvised, their weapons are borrowed, and you'd best get out of their way.
When the price of your sins comes due, the Church of Deals is there to collect.
Some sky steeds break from the thundering herd to ride free on the open winds.
Grief is a crucible where resolve is tempered.
"No harm can come to me while the Worldsoul shelters me."
Any challenge to Azorius authority is met with swift and potent retribution.
"Before I let you wield one of these, let's see you dodge one!"

"Many wings haunt the skies these days. Few of them bear good tidings."
—Lavinia

"The call came, spell-borne through mortar and stone to the ear of every soldier. The call came, and the advantage was ours."
—Lodusz, captain of the watch
"Some bend the law. I tie it into knots."

"I hear that Boros is losing its angels to the Gateless Movement. I'm sure this comes as no surprise to you."
—Teysa, to Lazav
Its fickle form holds hints of a thousand former identities.
". . . and furthermore . . ."

"About the sphinx, I have mixed feelings. Their wisdom I crave, but their secrecy I can't tolerate."
—Szadek
"Four parts molten bronze, yes ... one part frozen mercury, yes, yes ... but then what?"
Simic mages create redundant backups of their experiments to reduce the consequences of catastrophe.
The Izzet specialize in unnatural disaster.
"They've got eyes inside my head!"

"Hop away now, little Eternal. Go eat some flies."
—Kasmina
"This one opens the grate outside Zelzo Base. This one is for Ismeri Library. This one is for an invisible door . . . No, I've said too much."

"When your enemy flees, send the sea to pursue them."
—Kiora

"Most compete for insects at street level. Some dwell near Izzet laboratories and ride the thermal updrafts."
—Yolov, Simic bioengineer
Rumors float through the city like crows, alighting on citizens seemingly at random.

"We're on the fortieth floor, with one window, no balcony. No one could possibly get in."
—Minosz, Orzhov chief of security
"My greatest creation—me!"
"When properly invoked, the plasma globule encloses the offensive spell with a satisfying slurp."
A skilled Izzet chronarch can carry out an epic vendetta between the fall of one hourglass grain and the next.
Genius is finding the edge of what's possible, then jumping over it.
"Well, at least all of that arm-waving and arcane babbling you did was impressive."

"Your deed cannot be undone. You, however, can be."
—Agosto, Azorius imperator

"We have intel that some guilds have fallen under an invader's influence. Until we're sure, no venture succeeds."
—Lazav
He unmakes the world in his own image.
Fblthp had always hated crowds.
"There's no need to sound the alarm. You are minding your post admirably. I am authorized. All is well."

"The pain of searing iron and razor edges pales beside the pleasure of performance."
—Judith

"Even rats hoard their treasures. Are your precious things so different?"
—Izoni
Greatness, at any cost.
By design, the sarcophagus muffles the debtors' moans but does not silence them.

"You're right. I'm sure your Legion friends *are* looking for you. And once we've hidden a piece of you in each district, they'll get to keep looking for a long time."
—Ivrelya, Dimir spymaster
The feline Eternal felt Liliana's command, looked at her disdainfully, flicked its paw, and scampered away across the rooftops.
"The suffering of others is not my concern."
"Allow me a moment to catch your breath."

"All dead move to the hollow rhythm of necromancy."
—Savra
When he reaches for his key ring, you should be running for the exit.
Ravnica's safest strongholds are often neither.
No one welcomes his visit, yet all must grant him tribute.
"You'll pay what you owe, with your money or your life."
"My power is generosity, in a way. I give my survivors an appreciation for their lives."
The Orzhov are not the only religious tradition on Ravnica, nor the oldest.
As the bounty on Massacre Girl rose, so did the number of imitators.

"Let him be an example to others who would default on their debts to us."
—"The Cozen," Orzhov assassin
The undercity is always hungry.
In theory, the Guildpact keeps guild feuds from spiraling out of control. Personal feuds, however, are not covered.
Each soul he devours adds its hunger to his own.
Seen through Rakdos eyes, a cruel betrayal is a hilarious stunt.
Some storms never blow over.
The star performer of the Juri Revue, his shows have fans and blood spilling into the street.
"Subtlety is for lawmages and spies."

"From a great bonfire at the dawn of time, the first Gruul kindled their rage. The same flame burns in you."
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
"This day will end in death, but not the one you hoped for. This day will end in victory, but not the one you expected."
The ostentatious splendor of the Orzhov church was just asking to be smashed.

"For every inch of land they take from us, we take it back or we burn it. Give them nothing."
—Aurelia
Few have seen the inner workings of Ravnica's furnaces, but neighboring districts catch brief glimpses in the horrors that escape the flames.
He wants to watch Ravnica burn, one soul at a time.

"I see countless worlds. What makes them think I can't find them in just one?"
—Ral Zarek

"He displays a perverse charisma fueled by avarice. Highly dangerous. Recommend civil sanctions."
—Agmand Sarv, Azorius hussar
Krenko's hirelings are unflinchingly loyal.

"Places, everyone!"
—Judith
Scream: muffled. Pockets: emptied. Neck function: never the same again.

"The maaka remain loyal to us in this time of strife. We don't even have to feed them—our enemies do."
—Nedja, Gruul shaman
Each small blaze she sets jogs her memory, letting her piece together the mystery of her own fiery end.
Going to a Rakdos show is dangerous. Trying to leave early can be fatal.
The lawmage's argument was clever and well reasoned, but Blunk's response proved irrefutable.
Something roams the killing places, sniffing the guilt of the slayers, stalking them on iron paws.
The taste of blood breaks down what little self-control the Rakdos possess.
"That giant didn't even see me, let alone catch me! And I was close enough to smell him! Of course, that's not saying much."
The fear of dragons is as old and as powerful as the fear of death itself.
"By all means, take another step toward the captain."

"We fight to stop a tyrant, but we also fight for the gentle creatures who have no concept of what befalls their world."
—Vivien Reid
In times of peril, the vision the ancient paruns had for their city comes into focus.
Long ago, birds of paradise littered the skies. Thanks to the city's sprawl, most now exist as pets of society's elite.
The Street Swarm is the labor class that drives the Golgari's endless cycle of life and death.
"How truly vast this city must be, that I have traveled so far and seen so much, yet never once found the place where the buildings fail."
Saprolings add the three and the four to the "one-two punch."

"We're planting the seeds of change. Sometimes, we plant them in people."
—Vorel of the Hull Clade
The druid knew only one spell, a charm to encourage rapid plant growth. When airborne Eternals invaded her arboretum, she had to get creative.

"We're all food for something in the end."
—Cevraya, Golgari shaman
Man's best fungus.
Simic's strength comes from its diversity.

"The Selesnya are gathering armies. Do you still believe they aren't preparing for war?"
—Teysa, to Isperia
His work determines who is remembered and who feeds the worms.

"If you don't have a destination in mind, the route is all that matters."
—Tamina, district guide
"Let the song of Selesnya be heard above the rhythm of our thundering hordes!"

"Meat *and* eggs. We eat!"
—Borborygmos
Tumult is its natural habitat.
Suddenly, all the haggling didn't seem so important.
Street folk call them "spire mice," but behind the mockery is an unspoken envy of the ledgewalkers' skill at avoiding harm.
Whoever wins, the neighborhood loses.

"The Gruul embrace all things poisonous and living in the cracks of society."
—Teysa Karlov
Some use magic to spy through walls. Others use it to crush them.
"I can call an army to my side in the blink of an eye. Best not blink."
Centaurs are sent to evangelize in Gruul territories where words of war speak louder than prayers of peace.
"Your life serves a higher purpose now: ensuring the continuation of my own."
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
"Just as leaves fall and the tree blooms again, one day I will fall and the Conclave will endure."
Some of Orzhov's cruelest collectors remember their debtors by taste alone.
"Everyone deserves a day in court."
In Rakdos-controlled neighborhoods, everyone is part of the show.

"This footlight's broken. Get me a stagehand!"
—Judith

"Hold on to your ideals. They'll be tested more than your armor or the edge of your blade."
—Tajic
"Your arrival was expected...and unwelcome."
From death she grows living grandeur.
Lyzolda's pet rats eat better than the average citizen. In fact, they can usually be found eating the average citizen.
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."
"We gather the past from surface dwellers and sell it right back to them."

"It misses nothing and it has no sense of humor."
—Barvisa, courtroom scribe
"Does Teysa think me blind to her scheming? Ambition runs in our family."
"I told Jace that Ravnica would fall apart if he didn't take his responsibilities seriously. I didn't want to be right."
Though less well-known than its army of soldiers, the Boros Legion's mage-priests are as respected by the innocent as they are hated by the ghosts of the guilty.
Despite their stake in the city's survival, Rakdos cultists are loath to pass up any opportunity to sow chaos.
When giant sinkholes opened across Ravnica, they revealed buried oceans and the merfolk, once thought to be extinct.

"Touched by moroii"
—Undercity slang meaning "to grow old"
Dimir's best agents hide from death itself.
During their ascent to spirithood, patriarchs of Orzhova shed both flesh and emotion. This earthly slag is collected and formed into thrulls.

"Three daggers left in an angel's back, three enforcers with memory loss, three keys stolen from my own belt—and you talk of peace?"
—Tajic, to Aurelia
It departs through the streets' fissures with a sound like gravel pouring into a pond.

"Look at this creature, so like the Conclave it serves. Cut one head and it grows two. Damage it and it flourishes."
—Veszka, Selesnya evangel

"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process."
—Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
Ever wonder why you never see an old Rakdos cultist?
Some view Domri's unlikely ascent as a sign of Ilharg the Raze-Boar's imminent return.
"Nature's most raw beauty is the circle: perfect in its continuance, with no break between death and life."
They inflict pain to forget their own and break foes to feel whole.
"The clamor of the city drowns all voices. But together we can sing a harmony that will resonate from Ravnica's tallest spires to her deepest wells."

"I do not know which gives me more pride: the legions of soldiers marching in thunderous lockstep, or the cry of the skyknights riding their rocs like jagged lightning overhead."
—Razia

"It makes better use of Uncle Dragi's head than he ever did."
—Pesha, retired blacksmith
Azorius sphinxes are loyal to the precepts of the law, not to any particular guildmaster—even one of their own kind.
"Let the knowledge of absolute law inspire you to live a life of absolute order."
Quyzl was told by his mentor to "make more time" for his studies.
"You take our wilds, we take your city."
"Selesnya's soil is sacred, and you're about to meet it with your face."

"It is technically an ooze, but its lifespan measures only seconds. In that short time, its appetite for magic is extraordinary."
—Simic research notes
He has a job to finish, and it's you.
They are the voice of the wild, crying out with nature's fury and bringing forth its primeval might.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.

"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride."
—Agrus Kos
Dimir mages put the lanterns to good use, creating shapeshifters and sleeper agents from mana foreign to them.
Those without a guild signet often display a different form of protection.
It *wants* to remain a mystery, banishing the curious in favor of less inquisitive company.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
Gruul territorial markings need not be legible. The blood, snot, and muck used to smear them are unmistakably Gruul.
It's easy to believe you're a god when you're twice as powerful as everyone else.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
One man's trash is another man's troller.
The sigil holds different meanings depending on its form and presentation. While some wear it as a sign of status, others wear it as a sign of debt.
To bear the shield of the pariah is the highest honor a Boros can receive—and the last.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.

"I'd rather see the guilds contend together with words in the halls of power, than in the streets with swords."
